input.answer: The project did not actively re-center because backtests showed frequent narrowing (re-centering) destroyed value. While the narrow strategy earned 4x more fees, the impermanent loss (IL) and re-centering costs exceeded those gains. Consequently, the passive wide strategy outperformed the narrow one in 720-day walk-forward tests, even within flat market regimes.

input.question: Why did the LP earn less in fees during an uptrend than in a flat market?
input.reference: Fees accrue only while the price is inside the range and fee yield scales roughly with 1/width, so a narrow range earns much more in a flat market but is left behind in a trend, while a wide range stays in range but earns several times less; the journal states this mechanism (the basis of FlatWide) but has no live measurement of fees during an uptrend, and it attributes the backtest losses in up windows to impermanent loss and LVR rather than to lower fees.
input.answer: In an uptrend, a narrow LP earns more fees but suffers large LVR (Loss-Versus-Rebalancing): arbitrageurs trade against the position at stale prices, and the realized IL plus rotation costs exceed the fees collected. In a flat market, price stays near the LP’s range, so LVR is minimal and fees accumulate without offsetting losses. The journal confirms this: "wąska zbiera więcej fees ($1,316) ale umiera na IL od trendu (klasyczny LVR)" and "okna UP = klęska" while "FLAT = nasza nisza".

input.question: What does the function fetchFreshPool do?
input.reference: It re-reads the pool state on-chain (factory.getPool, then slot0 and liquidity) right before the mint step of a rebalance or rotation, so the new position is built from the current price instead of the price captured when the modal opened, and falls back to the old pool if the lookup fails; it was added after the 11.09 widening failed once on 'Price slippage check' and was never exercised live, since the only later chance (a FLAT_NARROW card on 16.09) was not signed and the positions were closed by hand in Uniswap.
input.answer: fetchFreshPool (in src/utils/uniswap.ts) re-fetches a pool's current on-chain state: it calls factory.getPool, then reads slot0 and liquidity to build a new Pool object with the same tokens and fee tier. It is fail-open: if the factory or RPC call fails, it returns the old pool object instead of throwing. It is wired into useRebalanceExecution and useRotateExecution just before buildMintStep, so rebalance/rotate executions use fresh price/liquidity data. A known caveat is that the range ticks still come from the original plan (computed at the old price), so after a price move the range is slightly off-center.
